title: Preface

teacherSummary.text: The 1818 Preface (written by Percy Shelley in Mary's voice) claims the central event is not impossible according to some physiologists, insists the story aims to show 'the amiableness of domestic affection,' and recalls the ghost-story origin.

context.history: Prefaces in the period often defended novels against charges of immorality or absurdity. Erasmus Darwin, mentioned here, was a well-known physician and poet who speculated about life.

significance: The Preface sets up the tension between scientific plausibility and moral fable that runs through the whole work.
discussionQuestions: Why might an author defend the 'possibility' of a fantastic event before the story begins?
Where does tone / mood appear in this chapter, and what effect does it have? Point to one passage.
How does this chapter connect to the book's larger concern with creation and responsibility?

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “the amiableness of domestic affection, and the excellence of universal virtue” slowly and put it in my own words: The 1818 Preface says the story aims to show the loveliness of family affection and the excellence of universal virtue. Next, craft. I notice two balanced phrases of praise, "amiableness of domestic affection" and "excellence of universal virtue," which sound reassuring and moral. The strongest word is “domestic”: it names the family love the creature will be shut out of. Then, effect. What does the Preface promise the novel will show readers? My answer: The Preface frames the book as moral, yet the novel will show what happens when someone is denied that domestic affection; the promise sets up the irony of the creature's exclusion.
